column2: Build the vertical selector as the site's entry view - the FIRST thing a visitor sees, ahead of the hero. Founder-confirmed; specified in DESIGN.md §4 "Vertical selector - the site's entry view". Read design-refs/REFERENCES.md and OPEN design-refs/strips/Clary_Selector.png before writing anything: "Are you a..." centred on a clean light ground, one pill per vertical (Museums & Galleries / Gyms), hover colourises the pill, and on selection the tab DRIFTS TO THE TOP RIGHT while the chosen view FADES IN CLEANLY, the tab staying there as the switch control. You are judged on distance from that 10/10 reference, not on being better than best. Three attached decisions in §4: remember the choice locally so returning visitors are not re-gated; retire the existing in-hero switcher so there is one control rather than two; and NEVER gate content from a deep link or a crawler - every existing floor loads / and expects the page, and tests/gimmicks.spec.ts drives the hero-tab-museums and hero-tab-gyms testids, so those must keep working wherever the control now lives. Freeze all of it under prefers-reduced-motion. REQUIRED TESTIDS, non-negotiable because the capture harness drives them: vertical-selector on the gate, select-museums and select-gyms on the two choices. Both previous attempts were rejected partly because the critic could not see past the gate at all - three of the reference's five assertions were unverifiable from the captures - so without these your work cannot be judged. Note also that the entry screen sitting ahead of the hero is NOT a D3 regression; §7 now says so explicitly, and the previous rejection on that ground was a rubric fault, not yours.
